name: Privacy dashboard and report
plain: A system view that shows which apps used sensitive data and when.
meaning: Lets users audit access to location, camera and mic. iOS also logs network contact.

android.persistence: Last 24 hours at launch; later releases extend
android.note: Apps can add attribution tags to explain access.

ios.prompt_ui: Settings > Privacy & Security > App Privacy Report
ios.store_policy: App privacy details in App Store Connect
ios.note: Shows data access, sensor use and domains contacted.

limits.headline: Can show you which apps used location, camera or mic, and when
limits.user_action: You open the Privacy dashboard in Settings, or App Privacy Report on iPhone
can: List when apps used location, camera and microphone
Show the explanations apps add to their access (Android)
cannot: Block or stop any app on its own
Show access that happened before the log began
limits.differs: iPhone also logs network domains contacted; Android shows an access timeline with app explanations.

story.what_it_is: A system screen showing which apps used your location, camera or mic, and when.

marketing.name: Privacy dashboard
marketing.pitch: See which apps accessed your location, camera and microphone, and change access in one place.

marketing.name: App Privacy Report
marketing.pitch: See how apps use the data and sensors you gave them, and which sites they contact.

story.for_you: A timeline shows each app that used the camera or mic and at what time. You can tap an app and turn off its access. A green dot on screen also tells you a sensor is live.
story.for_makers: Apps know they are watched, so most keep their sensor use honest. It also gives the platform a quick way to show users what happened. Makers must explain unusual use before a user spots it.

use_cases.example: A person sees a flashlight app used the mic at 3 am and removes it.
A parent checks which apps used the camera on a child's phone.
A free game is found to use location every few minutes.
A researcher shows an SDK calling home at odd hours.
A user checks that a health app does not read location all day.
IT checks sensor use by work apps.
A developer adds notes so the dashboard explains why the app uses location.

story.android_note: Android apps can add attribution tags that explain access in the dashboard.
story.ios_note: iOS also logs network contact, such as the domains an app talks to.
